executiveSummary.summary: API contract validation reveals critical gaps across the microservices architecture. Only identity-service has authentication enforced via HTTP Basic; all other services use permitAll(). Six of 16 services are empty placeholders (cart, content, risk, search, support, registry-center). The ai-service is the largest but 85% of its 112 endpoints are fully open. No API gateway or centralized auth exists. Services lack standardized error responses, pagination, and consistent status codes.

issues: Some GET endpoints accept request bodies (non-standard)
Used for cancel, approve, publish, capture, fail — should be PUT or PATCH in RESTful design
Underused — quotation update, vendor update, config update
Missing — should be used for partial updates
CORS preflight not configured in any service
No HEAD endpoints for resource existence checks

findings.usage: Default success for GET, POST, PUT
issues: Overused — 201 for creation rarely returned; most POST endpoints return 200
Some controllers use 201, most don't specify status code
Custom error body varies; no standardized format
HTTP Basic handles 401 but no custom 401 handler

findings.usage: Should be used for role-based access
issues: Not explicitly returned by any controller
Not consistently implemented — many controllers return null/empty instead of 404
Not used anywhere — no duplicate detection
Not used — 400 used for all validation failures
Default Spring error returned; could leak stack traces

findings.detail: Many request DTOs lack validation annotations
Some use @RequestParam, some use path variables inconsistently
Some endpoints don't enforce Content-Type header
No consistent ApiError or ErrorResponse DTO across services
List endpoints return raw arrays without pagination info
No @JsonIgnore on sensitive fields; no field-level filtering
No @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) configured globally; nulls leak in responses
Some use camelCase, some use snake_case — no naming convention enforced
